newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices flat, focus on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- Prices flat, focus on FOMC.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices opened mostly unchanged as players who expected no action out of Tuesday's Federal Reserve policy makers' meeting kept an eye on it anyway.

"I don't think a lot of people are looking at this (Federal Open Market Committee Meeting) to see if rates are going to be unchanged for the day, but obviously it's on a lot of people's minds," one trader said.
Another trader agreed that the Fed is likely to stand pat on rates, but said potential comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan could spur activity.

"Right now the probability is like 80 percent that he is not going to do anything. If he does something, then you are in trouble," the trader said. "Other than that, he might just say something like we've just got to be cautious, inflation could turn around..."
The trader said while the market opened unchanged, a thin new issue calendar could help prices move higher.
"There's not much coming on the calendar," he said. "That's going to help some of these dealers."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 1/32 at 98-4/32 to yield 6.52 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was up 5/32 at 120-10/32. The September T-bond contract was up 2/32 at 114-5/32. The MOB spread was 197 ticks.
As for Tuesday's new muni issues, offerings are expected to total $474 million in 31 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings are expected to total $235 million in 12 sales, with a $46 million Texas Housing Agency offering through John Nuveen & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 19 sales totaling $239 million are scheduled. A $62 million Fort Bend Independent School District, Texas, offering was the largest.
An additional five sales totaling $80 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues Tuesday depending on market conditions.
